svg.title: TOPAK H9 — The corpus's specifications form a graph: layers are open, every edge is typed by what it leaves to a person, a guarantee carries its givens, and a theorem is inherited at the grade of its weakest edge
svg.desc: ADR-0057 (Proposed, 2026.11.06; R1 2026.11.07) reads the corpus's four separate keepers of "what discharges what" (the drift pins, the binding table, the manifests, the sync scripts) as one graph: artifacts are nodes with an open set of layers ⟨K1⟩, every edge is one of eight types ordered by what it leaves to a person ⟨K2⟩, each edge is a premise, and a theorem holds at a grade. ADR-0058 (Proposed, 2026.11.06) gives a deployment the same graph as an overlay: keep, replace, add or omit each node, type every edge it re-establishes, publish its inventory at every grade, and report upstream what the archetype lacks ⟨K4⟩. Both are Proposed and nothing here is in force: the graph is built and its checker has run (419 nodes, 435 edges, built at 9749dfa + working tree; results of 2026.11.07), the three dependent entries are drafted and pending, clause pins are not run in drift.rs, and no overlay ADR-0058 describes is computed. The graph in this tree is the build of 2026.11.07: it holds neither the overlay's eight modules nor the Workflow and Mesh proofs (G12 item 111).

svg.text: Proposed means nothing here is in force. The custodian settled five things on 2026.11.06: the set of layers is open ⟨K1⟩; inheritance is graded ⟨K2⟩; the graph carries no brand name ⟨K3⟩; there are two records, ADR-0057 for the corpus and ADR-0058 for adopters and the ecosystem ⟨K4⟩; both are prescriptive, saying what to produce and what the corpus does, should do and could do ⟨K5⟩. Every other choice is the drafter's. C2 applies to both because each makes an exhaustiveness claim (every relation the corpus relies on is an edge;

every edge an inventory relies on is in the overlay); C4 applies to ADR-0057 because three open-list items (G11 56, 90, 103) become computed. Nothing in ADR-0057 changes a theorem, a premise or a verdict at the reference: at grade *trusted* its inventory is the one inventory.py computes today (§5; the checker confirms it theorem by theorem). One author, one day, for both; R1 built and not reviewed.

text.tspan: What the picture is, and is not

svg.text: Seventeen of 435 edges, chosen by the diagram around Seats, the only module whose theorems have a route to the code besides the row (§4), and around the strongest edge, ⑮, which ends at a node
not in force (finding 6). An edge runs from a lower node to the node it discharges (§3).
5 of the eight stale edges are drawn (⑦, ⑧, ⑨, ⑩, ⑬), in red. Every module's edge up to its record is *read*, by the drafter (finding 10); only four are drawn.
Layers are labels for reading and carry no premise (§1); the picture stacks the five that have nodes. The assurance layer's rows are not nodes: a *trusted* edge's lower end is a row (§3).

text.tspan: How a theorem's grade is read off the picture (§5)

svg.text: OnlyThinkersAuthor and OneSeatPerPrincipal are invariant(Seats) by ① and refines(Seats) by ⑤, or by ⑦ + ⑧ (model-faithful(apply/Seats)). Their grade is the strongest, over the
routes that hold, of each route's weakest edge: ⑤ holds, so *trusted*; the Lean route is stale, so no higher.
At grade *trusted* the inventory is today's: 19 of 43 of Annex B hold, the same theorems inventory.py holds. No theorem of Annex B holds at any grade above *trusted* (the results file's "held at
each grade").

A node is an artifact that states something normative or checks something stated: a record's clause, a module, a proof module, a Lean file, a floor stage, a Rego policy, a crate or a function in it, a schema. Named by its path, or by record and section; its content identified by digest.

The set of layers is open ⟨K1⟩. A new kind of artifact is given a layer name when it first enters the graph, and no record is needed to add one *(drafter's choice: a layer carries no premise; only edges do, §4)*.
No name beyond its description, *the specification graph* ⟨K3⟩.

text.tspan: The clause is the binding point above the model layer (§2)

svg.text: A numbered subsection of a record's Decision, with its inline amendments, cited as the corpus already cites it ("ADR-0031 §4, A1"). Records are append-only with typed History rows, so a clause's number is stable. A clause may number its
guarantees §n.k.
Records already ratified are not rewritten. Their givens are read from the binding table, their discharge from the graph. A clause gains the four parts when an amendment next touches it.

text.tspan: gives each clause four parts, in this order (§2)

svg.text: Goal. One sentence: why the clause exists. Not normative, and not bound.
Givens. What the guarantees rest on: rows, parameters, derived premises and other clauses, by id. "None beyond BASE" is a claim, stated as one.
Guarantees. The normative statements, numbered.

Discharge. The edges that discharge each guarantee (§3), with their types, or "none yet", stated as a claim. Named *discharge* and not *gate* *(drafter's choice; the custodian proposed "gates")*: the corpus already has floor gates and
promotion gates, and a record's own gate is its Ratification condition.

text.tspan: A citation is not an edge (§3)

svg.text: A record citing another, or code citing a record in a comment, discharges nothing; it is how a reader finds the edge.

text.tspan: A read edge names its reader (§3)

svg.text: A reading by the drafter and a reading by someone else are the same type, and the graph shows which it was (ADR-0053 R1(b),
Mutations and witnesses (ADR-0046) support a reading: they show the module tells the clause from its negation, not that it reads
the clause rightly. They do not change the edge's type.

text.tspan: An edge is fresh or stale (§3)

svg.text: It pins the content of both ends: by clause for records (§7), by digest otherwise. An edge whose pin no longer matches is stale,
and is re-pinned by the review drift.rs already asks for: read the change, bring the lower node into line or register why not,
then re-pin.
The builder keeps an edge's pins until --repin names it: re-pinning is the review (the docstring).

text.tspan: The method is the corpus's choice; the type is not (§10)

svg.text: Which formalism states a node is chosen by the kind of property: a protocol in TLA+, an authorization in Cedar, a functional core
in Lean, a data shape in a schema.
Some components cannot be specified, and the architecture keeps them outside the verified object (ADR-0007,
ADR-0016): nodes with no edge below the record, so every theorem that would need one is computed void rather than assumed.
A new method enters with its toolchain row (ADR-0045 §4).

text.tspan: 3 · Each edge is a premise (§4), a theorem is inherited at a grade (§5), and the rest of the decision (§6–§9, §13)
Each edge contributes a named premise (§4)

svg.text: An edge of type *t* from *x* to *y* contributes edge(t, x → y), a premise column of kind check (ADR-0053 R7): its value is the edge's freshness and, where the type has a
results file, that file's verdict. A stale edge's premise is false. An absent edge's premise is false, as an undeclared row is (ADR-0045 §3, rule 1).
ADR-0053's derived premises become instances, and nothing they compute changes: invariant(M) is T-0045-31, or T-0045-37 with edge(proved of a reading,
encoding(M) → M); refines(Seats) is T-0045-28, or the route through SeatsModel.
T-0045-28 becomes a derived premise for every theorem whose route reaches the code: the row, or any route of edges from the implementation to the module. Today the
row is the only route for every theorem but the two of Seats, so no verdict moves. The graph's binding section holds 41 derived premises, reaches-code(…) among them.
An edge is added with its premise in the same commit, and inventory.py --check passes before it lands.

text.tspan: A theorem is inherited at a grade; each grade is a binary inventory (§5 ⟨K2⟩)

svg.text: A grade is an edge type used as a threshold. The inventory at grade *g* is ADR-0023 §2's inventory computed with every edge premise of a type weaker than *g* set false. A
theorem holds at *g* when it is present there; its grade is the strongest *g* at which it holds: over the routes that hold, the strongest of each route's weakest edge. Rows,
parameters and gap premises hold or fail as today.
At grade *trusted* the inventory is the one the corpus computes today. Raising the grade can only void a theorem, never revive one. ADR-0023 §2 holds at every grade:
present or absent, no weaker version.
Graded on its way down *(drafter's choice)*: over the edges from the layer a theorem is stated at to the layer that runs. The edges up, from a module to its record, are
graded once per module and reported beside the inventory: every one is *read* today, by the drafter (finding 5).

text.tspan: A guarantee stated twice is two nodes and an edge (§6)

svg.text: The graph holds both and the typed edge between them. The operator envelope (I47 (e)) is a Cedar node and a Rust node with a *tested* edge. The checker lists every such
pair with its type, so each is raised (generated from the other, or proved equal) or kept with the type showing. Listing is this record's obligation; raising is not.
The checker lists the operator's envelope, C1 to C9 (ADR-0050 §4; mechanism/ I47 (e)) (band 5).
The drift pins move from whole files to clauses for records: a record's pin is the digest of each clause the reference follows, by section, with its inline amendments. A History
row, a status line or a pending amendment not yet inline changes no clause and trips no pin. Modules, floor files and code stay pinned by file. drift.rs's rule that every cited
record or module is pinned is kept, read by clause.
A debt against ADR-0033, not a change to it: ADR-0033 A18 is drafted (2026.11.07) and pending; it records no run. spec/clauses.py splits and pins a record's clauses
(finding 9b).

text.tspan: One graph, and the four lists are read against it (§8)

svg.text: One machine-readable file under spec/, of nodes and typed edges, each with its pins and evidence by digest. A checker computes every stale edge; every clause with
guarantees and no discharging edge; every twice-stated guarantee; and, through inventory.py, the inventory at each grade with each theorem's grade and route.
Checked against it first, generated from it later *(drafter's choice)*: corpus-pins.sha256, the binding JSON's check columns, the manifest index and the sync scripts' file
lists each gain a check that they agree with the graph. The binding table stays canonical for its row premises.

text.tspan: Interfaces are a layer (§9); the trusted base (§13)

svg.text: A format gains an interface node, with a machine-readable schema, when a record next touches it *(drafter's choice: not a sweep)*: JSON Schema for a lease, an allowlist
entry, a tool result; AsyncAPI for a topic and its records. Its edges run to the clause that defines it and from the code and the floor that read it. The interface layer has no node
today.
No row is added (§13). The checker decides no admit, promotion or issuance; its failure can misstate a grade, a claim about evidence and not an addition of authority. A grade
is only as good as the graph, as a verdict is only as good as the declaration.

The checker ran 2026.11.07 on the graph built at 9749dfa + working tree (419 nodes, 435 edges). Well formed: yes. Result line: "graph well formed, the four lists agree, and the inventory at grade trusted is inventory.py's · 8 stale edges · 2 premise-route verdicts moved by stale edges". It exits 1 if the graph is malformed, a list disagrees with it, or the inventory at grade *trusted* differs from inventory.py's for Annex B; stale edges and a premise route that differs are reported, not failed on (the docstring). The graph was built at
9749dfa and does not hold the overlay's modules or the Workflow and Mesh proofs (G12 item 111); every count here is of that build.

svg.text: Not taken ⟨K3⟩

Positive. The corpus can say how strongly each theorem reaches the code, not only whether its premises are declared. Staleness is computed: what G11 lists by hand at items 56, 90 and 103 the checker reports. History rows stop tripping the drift test, and a changed clause
still does. Twice-stated guarantees are listed with the type of the edge that ties them. Adopters get an interface (ADR-0058) built on what the corpus already does.

Negative. One more artifact to keep in step, with its own checker, beside four it does not yet replace. The total order may be wrong in places (finding 4), and every grade inherits the error. Grades will look worse than the prose: most mechanism theorems grade *trusted*
today, which is true and has been stated only in T-0045-28's note. One author, one day, as every record since G2.
The graph, the checker, and the dependent entries (§14): built, run and drafted ⟨R1⟩. Two things remain: the commit that carries them, and the custodian's reading of findings 7 and 8.
The custodian's reading of every drafter's choice, above all the order of §3 and the downward grading of §5.
Who reads the edges up. Finding 5 is the bootstrap reviewer's question in another form (ADR-0029 A2).
The archetype-evolution record (unwritten) owns the graph's versioning, as it owns the binding table's.
Narrative. The ToO and the glossary owe *specification graph*, *edge type*, *grade*, *givens*, *discharge* and *stale edge* at the next cut.

1. The paper's levels are properties of edges. Spec-as-source is the floor's edge; anchored by proof the admit decision's; by replay apply's; by tests the operator path's; spec-first the workflow path's, for now.
2. The rule that a stale edge is false is already in the corpus, for ADR-0053 R7's check premises. This record extends a rule; it does not make one.

3. Graded inheritance and ADR-0023 §2. §5 keeps "no weaker version" by taking a binary inventory per threshold. A C3 reviewer may still read a grade as partial credit; the record that settles it is ADR-0023's.

4. The order of §3 is not obviously total. *Executed* and *generated* each leave one tool; *proved of a reading* and *replayed* leave different things. If a pair is incomparable, the grade becomes per axis.

5. Every module is a reading of a record, by the drafter. The corpus's strongest results sit on its weakest edge type at the top, as the code sits on T-0045-28 at the bottom. The checkpoints have said so since G2.

6. The strongest edge points at a node not in force. The reference executes the workflow stage, which is Proposed (G11 item 102). A grade measures the edge, not the standing of its ends; the graph shows both.

7. §14's third condition cannot be met as worded on today's tree, and §4 says why ⟨R1⟩. The Lean route of refines(Seats) names stale edges (item 103); with T-0045-28 excluded the two Seats theorems are void by the graph. Which of two readings meets it is the
custodian's choice.

8. Two edges reach the code and are not counted as routes ⟨R1⟩: the executed edge and FloorRefinement's proof, both "route": false. FloorRefinement is one step, not the module's behaviours (ADR-0053 §5 R2). Whether the executed edge is a route is the custodian's
choice.

9. The drafter's choices in building ⟨R1⟩. (a) Pins: a read edge from the code or a trusted edge pins its upper end only, as corpus-pins.sha256 does; pinning both would stale 139 read edges on every commit. (b) Clauses: a record without a Decision is one clause, text;

unnumbered subsections, annexes and ADR-0033's ## 7. are clauses; a pending subsection is left out, pending text inline stays in. (c) Admit-results edges pin every file mechanism/lean transcribes. (d) The graph check is *proved*; a Lean proof of an encoding is *proved of a
reading*. (e) Theorems no module states are stated at STATED_AT's nodes.
10. Every module's edges up are *read*, by the drafter ⟨R1⟩: all 31 modules. Finding 5, computed.
11. 51 clauses of 12 records the reference follows have no edge but the code's reading ⟨R1⟩. Some are by nature outside any model (§10); the list is where to look for the rest.

svg.text: Adopting TOPAK is already a declaration (the Adopter's Guide §1): parameters moved (ADR-0023 §6), the rung per seat, the trusted-base rows instantiated (ADR-0045 §4). It says nothing about artifacts: an adopter who writes their own mechanism has no place to state what ties it to the modules; a supplier has no form in which to publish what its artifact discharges. ADR-0049 §4 already grades one schema in two grades, *checked* or *claimed*; ADR-0057 gives the corpus eight, and this record gives deployments and suppliers the
same ⟨K4⟩ (Context).

policy, a runtime monitor
The node and its edges, typed

Nothing; its edges are absent and their premises false

text.tspan: The archetype publishes its graph; a deployment's graph is an overlay on it (§1)

svg.text: The archetype's graph (ADR-0057 §8) is published with each archetype version, by digest. For each archetype node, one of four operations, and for each edge, a type. The reference is the first overlay (§9): it keeps every record and
module, and adds its crates.

text.tspan: A replaced node re-establishes its edges, each typed (§2)

svg.text: Every edge the archetype node had is re-established at a declared type, or declared absent. An edge not mentioned is absent, and its premise is false (ADR-0045 §3 rule 1, as ADR-0057 §4 reads it).

Re-establish at the strongest type you can. A replacement that reruns the archetype's checks against itself (the floor's gate suite, the trace replay, the graph check) takes the type of that check. One that does not takes *read*, with its reader
named, or is absent.

text.tspan: The method is the deployment's; the type follows from what it leaves (§3 ⟨K1⟩)

svg.text: P, Quint, Alloy, Dafny, Verus, Kani, Coq, Isabelle, or the corpus's own TLA+, TLAPS and Lean. A Verus proof that a Rust mechanism refines a module is *proved*, and its prover is a row.

A prover or checker the archetype has no row for is declared as a degeneracy under ADR-0023 §4a, a D-row beside the nearest archetype row (T-0045-29, T-0045-31 or T-0045-37), and reported upstream (§6): Annex A has no generic
row for a prover a deployment chose (finding 2).

text.tspan: Inheritance is graded, and the declaration publishes every grade (§4 ⟨K2⟩)

svg.text: The deployment's inventory is computed from its overlay, at every grade, as ADR-0057 §5 computes the corpus's. A claim made outside the declaration names its grade: "NoActionUnderFencedEpoch holds at *replayed*", not "holds". A

text.tspan: claim with no grade is read at *trusted*.

svg.text: Show each node's standing beside each grade: a deployment that executes a Proposed floor stage has a strong edge to a node not in force (ADR-0057 finding 6), and its declaration says both.
The composition note carries grades (ADR-0023 §7a): theorems whose grade falls by the joint effect of several overlay operations, computed from the overlay; an empty delta is still a claim.

text.tspan: A deployment may grade above the archetype; the admission test is unchanged (§5)

svg.text: A mechanism proved to refine the modules where the reference has T-0045-28 has the archetype's inventory at a higher grade. Not a capability the archetype lacks in ADR-0023 §4's sense (the inventory is not larger; the archetype stays the unique maximum). It is a route the archetype lacks, and it is reported
upstream (§6), so the archetype can add it as an alternative in the derived premise.

text.tspan: Report upstream what the archetype lacks (§6)

svg.text: A route stronger than the archetype's (§5); a method with no row (§3); a node every deployment of its kind will need, a schema above all (ADR-0057 §9); an edge it could not re-establish because the archetype node was underspecified. Each report is a finding about the archetype, as ADR-0023 §4's rejections
are.

text.tspan: Suppliers publish subgraphs, and a deployment imports them (§7)

svg.text: A supplier of a tool, a Persona, a policy library, a transport or a mechanism publishes its nodes by digest, the archetype nodes it claims to discharge, the edges with their types, and the evidence by digest. An imported edge keeps its type if the deployment reruns its check, and enters as *read*, with the
supplier as its reader, if it does not. ADR-0049 §4 is the case already in force.
Rerun what you can. A supplier's proof that a deployment re-checks is the deployment's proof; one it does not is the supplier's word. The form of a supplier's subgraph is owed (Open obligations).

text.tspan: Ungraded inheritance for adopters, graded for the corpus

svg.text: Rejected ⟨K2⟩. The same computation, or the two inventories cannot be compared

Positive. An adopter can say what ties their artifacts to the theorems, and at what strength, in a form the gate reads. Suppliers can publish what they discharge, and deployments can see what they rerun and what they take on word. The ecosystem feeds the archetype:
stronger routes, missing rows and missing schemas arrive as findings. A claim carries its grade, so "TOPAK-conformant" stops meaning one thing for a proof and another for a trust root.

Negative. A declaration is larger, and a deployment needs ADR-0057's checker to produce it. Graded claims invite grade-shopping: §4 asks the whole inventory to be published, and nothing stops a quotation from leaving it out. Everything rests on ADR-0057's order of types
(its finding 4).
1. ADR-0049 already grades declarations, for one schema and in two grades. This record is that distinction, generalized.
2. Annex A has no row for a prover a deployment chose. Every method beyond TLC, TLAPS and Lean enters as a degeneracy, which reads as a weakening even where it strengthens.
3. A deployment can exceed the archetype's grade and not its inventory. Grades are a second order on deployments, and the archetype is not its maximum.
4. The reference's strongest edge ends at a Proposed node (§9). Grade and standing are separate, and a declaration that shows one without the other misleads.
5. A supplier's evidence is one hand's, as the corpus's is (G11 §4). The reader on a *read* edge is how a deployment sees it.
ADR-0057, and its checker, on which every computation here rests.
The ADR-0023 amendment and the Guide's entries (§8).
The form of a supplier's subgraph, as a schema node (ADR-0057 §9).
